title: OmniControl: Control Any Joint at Any Time for Human Motion Generation
summary: Combines analytic spatial guidance and learned realism guidance for multi-joint control within text-to-motion diffusion.
method: Converts relative pose features to world-space joints for gradient-based spatial correction. A control network supplies realism residuals so constraints and whole-body coordination are refined together during denoising.
conditions: Text plus selected joints, keyframe times and target xyz positions. Quantitative controls come from ground-truth motion trajectories; manually authored constraints are demonstrated separately.
data_split: HumanML3D and KIT-ML use the cited Guo evaluation protocol. Models generate 196 frames; control densities are 1, 2, 5, 49 and 196 keyframes. No semantic-combination or subject holdout is newly established.
metrics: FID, R-precision and diversity assess distribution/text quality. Trajectory failure, location failure and average positional error assess constraints. Foot skating uses 2.5 cm displacement at foot height below 5 cm.
evaluation: Pelvis-only comparisons use matched constraints; all-joint and sampled joint-combination tests are separate. Appendix A.8 excludes KIT skating because the data lack reliable ground-height consistency.
limitations: Conflicting joint constraints can produce unnatural motion; skating remains and inference is expensive. GT trajectory control is a stronger information setting than text and initial state alone.
evidence_locator: §§3.1–3.3; §4 and Tables 1–3; Appendices A.4–A.5, A.8, A.10–A.11.

title: Guided Motion Diffusion for Controllable Human Motion Synthesis
summary: Adds spatial objectives to text-to-motion diffusion through emphasis projection, imputation and dense guidance.
method: Emphasis projection rebalances global root features against local pose features. Imputation enforces explicit known coordinates; dense guidance propagates sparse constraint gradients through the denoising prediction. A trajectory diffusion model can supply intermediate root paths.
conditions: Text and a differentiable objective, optionally a supplied complete trajectory, timed keyframe locations, target and 2D obstacle SDF. Different control modes provide different information.
data_split: HumanML3D supplies training and text-to-motion tests under the cited benchmark protocol. Trajectory-conditioned comparisons impute real test trajectories; keyframe and obstacle examples are separate. A new subject/compositional split is not specified.
metrics: FID, R-precision and diversity measure synthesis; trajectory/keyframe error and foot skating examine control. Constraint objectives and obstacle visualizations do not amount to a full contact-dynamics benchmark.
evaluation: §6 separates text-only, trajectory-conditioned, sparse-keyframe and obstacle tasks. Ablations examine root representation, emphasis and guidance rather than changing all conditions simultaneously.
limitations: Performance depends on the pretrained motion prior, representation and usable constraint gradients. Goal satisfaction can trade against naturalness. The method does not maintain articulated-object state across long manipulation tasks.

title: FineMoGen: Fine-Grained Spatio-Temporal Motion Generation and Editing
summary: Uses structured part/time descriptions and mixture attention for fine-grained generation and instruction-based editing.
method: Spatio-Temporal Mixture Attention builds global attention templates with explicit part/time influence and sparsely activated experts. An LLM modifies structured descriptions for editing, after which the diffusion model regenerates the sequence.
conditions: Fine-grained text assigned to body parts and temporal phases, with sequence length. Editing additionally uses prior description/context and an instruction; this is not arbitrary mesh-conditioned interaction.
data_split: HumanML3D, KIT-ML and BABEL complement HuMMan-MoGen: 2,968 videos, 160 action types and 102,336 annotations. The checked §4 reports test evaluations but does not give an independently auditable subject/recording split ratio for HuMMan-MoGen.
metrics: FID, R-precision, multimodal distance, diversity and multimodality use benchmark embeddings. Temporal composition tables compare text alignment and motion distributions; these metrics do not independently establish physical contacts.
evaluation: Tables 1–2 evaluate standard text-to-motion; Table 3 tests temporal composition; Table 4 is a zero-shot ablation without training on temporal-composition data. Evaluations repeat twenty times with reported intervals.
limitations: The structured description format restricts interfaces, and editing depends on LLM interpretation. A temporal-composition result should not be restated as an object-state or source-ancestry generalization test.

title: ReMoDiffuse: Retrieval-Augmented Motion Diffusion Model
summary: Reuses training-database motion and text examples inside diffusion rather than simply concatenating retrieved clips.
method: Hybrid retrieval combines CLIP semantic similarity and length-related kinematic compatibility. Semantic-modulated attention absorbs retrieved motion/text features; condition mixture combines text/retrieval/unconditional predictions with tuned weights.
conditions: Target text and expected motion length plus a retrieval database built from training examples. Retrieved motion is a reference condition; no future test trajectory is intended as input.
data_split: HumanML3D and KIT-ML benchmark train/test protocols are used. The retrieval store consists of training entities. Rarity is computed relative to training captions; this is not a separately constructed unseen skill-pair split.
metrics: FID, R-precision, multimodal distance, diversity and multimodality measure generation. Tail-5% MM distance and bin-balanced MM distance examine rare-caption behavior according to nearest training-text similarity.
evaluation: Standard test tables and retrieval/attention ablations are evaluated, with twenty repeated runs and confidence intervals. Rarity-stratified analysis distinguishes common from uncommon text conditions.
limitations: Database coverage and retrieved reference quality constrain benefits. Rarity in embedding space is not equivalent to semantic compositional novelty, and motion-distribution gains do not certify contact, dynamics or task completion.

title: Optimizing Diffusion Noise Can Serve As Universal Motion Priors
summary: Optimizes latent diffusion noise to satisfy editing, refinement and completion objectives without task-specific retraining.
method: Differentiates a motion-space objective through deterministic diffusion sampling. DDIM inversion initializes editing noise; normalized gradients and temporal noise decorrelation stabilize optimization and preserve the learned prior.
conditions: An input motion or noisy/partial observations and differentiable constraints. Editing experiments optimize without text conditioning, even when text originally generated the input motion.
data_split: Editing uses six input actions with sixteen random pelvis edits each, giving 96 edits. Refinement samples 300 HumanML3D test motions and adds 5 cm noise, including 6/8/10-joint partial observations.
metrics: Objective error measures target-joint distance; content preservation uses action-specific frame rules. Foot skating and jitter assess artifacts; refinement additionally reports MPJPE and FID against held-out motion features.
evaluation: Compares GMD and optimization-based priors, tests MDM/MLD/GMD backbones, and ablates gradient normalization and decorrelation. The small editing set and refinement test are distinct experiments.
limitations: Observation coverage and the underlying prior limit recovery. Unrealistic local optima remain possible, and optimization is slow: the stated editing setup takes roughly three minutes on a 3090.

title: PhysDiff: Physics-Guided Human Motion Diffusion Model
summary: Interleaves motion diffusion with a simulator-based imitation projection instead of applying physics only after generation.
method: A PPO-trained motion imitation policy tracks selected denoised estimates in IsaacGym. The projected simulated motion conditions subsequent diffusion steps; projection scheduling favors later, lower-noise stages.
conditions: Text or an action label and motion duration, together with a pretrained denoiser and imitation controller. SMPL body attributes condition tracking; PD targets and residual forces support imitation.
data_split: Text-to-motion uses HumanML3D. Action-to-motion uses HumanAct12 and UESTC sequences provided by the cited ACTOR protocol. The checked sections do not establish an independent semantic-combination or object-interaction split.
metrics: FID and text R-precision or action-classification accuracy assess generation. Penetrate and Float measure mesh-ground distances with 5 mm tolerance; Skate measures contacting-foot displacement. Phys-Err sums these distance quantities.
evaluation: Compares MDM/MotionDiffuse backbones, number and timing of projections, and postprocessing-only alternatives. Late-step projection is evaluated separately from simply increasing simulator calls.
limitations: Projection is expensive and depends on controller coverage. Residual-force-assisted simulation and ground-artifact metrics do not establish unassisted physical feasibility, object-contact correctness or hardware execution.

title: Unified Human-Scene Interaction via Prompted Chain-of-Contacts
summary: Compiles language into sequential body-joint/object-part contact constraints and executes them with one physics controller.
method: An LLM planner generates a Chain of Contacts with object, part, joint, contact type and relative direction. A task parser advances contact stages; PPO with an adversarial motion discriminator learns a common low-level policy.
conditions: Language, scene object/part descriptions and optional layouts for planning; meshes/point clouds, humanoid state and the contact plan for execution. Training uses pregenerated plans rather than end-to-end LLM optimization.
data_split: ScenePlan training uses 40 PartNet objects with generated steps. Evaluation uses 40 PartNet objects and ten ScanNet scenarios, with 1,040 and 100 plans. SAMP clips and twenty representative CIRCLE clips train the discriminator.
metrics: Success rate requires every plan stage within n×10 seconds. Contact error measures requested contact/noncontact joint-part distances; success steps and planner correctness supplement whole-plan success.
evaluation: Scenario, horizon, interaction and planner ablations assess the unified controller and LLM interface. Scanned-scene tests are separated from PartNet-derived synthetic layouts.
limitations: The framework only interacts with fixed objects and does not model moving/carrying objects. Reported object counts alone do not establish that train/evaluation PartNet identities are disjoint.

title: Towards Highly-Constrained Human Motion Generation with Retrieval-Guided Diffusion Noise Optimization
summary: Combines retrieved and random diffusion noise through task-aware spatial/temporal masks for difficult constraints.
method: Relational task parsing allocates constraints to retrieval and optimization. Separate retrieved/random noises are optimized, reward-guided masks select their mixture, and final DNO refines the combined initialization.
conditions: Differentiable constraint functions, optional text, a pretrained generator and a searchable motion database. Constraint difficulty/relationships can be manually specified or inferred by an LLM.
data_split: Base MDM-RoHM is trained on the HumanML3D training split, but retrieval uses the whole dataset. Tests define narrow-gap, low-barrier and counted-step tasks; these are not strict source-held-out retrieval evaluations.
metrics: Foot skating, maximum joint acceleration, constraint error and maximum scene penetration assess feasibility. Counted-step success, joint semantic success and pace score assess numerical/action consistency.
evaluation: Compares ProgMoGen+DNO and MaskControl under specified difficult constraints, including 0.4 m gaps. Spatial/temporal masks, retrieval, rewards, task parsing and task difficulty are ablated.
limitations: Adds several optimization phases and roughly 300 additional steps relative to DNO. Diversity contracts under severe constraints; unnatural motion and text misalignment remain possible. Whole-dataset retrieval limits independent generalization claims.

title: InteractAgent: Agentic Human Motion Interaction with Memory-Augmented Reflection
summary: Wraps a frozen motion executor with local visual recovery and cross-attempt planning reflection.
method: The same multimodal LLM performs scene analysis, planning, visual evaluation and reflection. A frozen Motion-Agent MotionLLM realizes action lists. Online observation chooses continue/redo/replan; inference-time memory informs later attempts without weight updates.
conditions: Scene images, high-level task text, rendered execution feedback and a frozen motion executor. Reconstructed scene geometry is still needed for rendering and independent penetration measurements.
data_split: Adapts UniHSI and TRUMANS scene/task resources. This is training-free orchestration; checked §4 does not provide a new train/test partition or an auditable per-complexity task inventory, so source split independence remains unspecified.
metrics: Execution/task success is reported by complexity. Physical validity uses body-scene SDF penetration, including maximum and highest-10%-frame mean, preventing long noninteractive intervals from diluting severe collisions.
evaluation: Tables 1–3 compare training-free variants, a supervised UniHSI-CoCo baseline, planner backbones and executors. Ablations separate online feedback from offline/memory reflection.
limitations: The planner and visual evaluator share a backbone, so reported success is not an independent physical certificate. Occlusion, view sampling, executor limits and retry cost remain; geometric penetration must be reported separately.
